##### NPSEM

A nonparametric structural equation model (NPSEM) is defined relative to a directed acyclic graph (@def-dag) on a random vector: each entry is a deterministic function of its parents in the graph and of its own error term, and the functions are not given a parametric form. The parameter is the set of functions together with the joint law of the error terms, on which the NPSEM itself places no restriction (@def-npsem). The same equations also say how the variables would be generated in hypothetical worlds in which some of them are set by intervention. An example of such a model is shown below. In this set of equations $(f_*)$, values that are produced by equations higher up in the list serve as inputs to equations lower down in the list.


$$
\begin{aligned}
L_1 &= f_{L_1}(U_{L_1}) \\
L_2 &= f_{L_2}(U_{L_2}, L_1) \\
L_3 &= f_{L_3}(U_{L_3}, L_1, L_2) \\
A_1 &= f_{A_1}(U_{A_1}, L_1, L_2, L_3) \\
A_2 &= f_{A_2}(U_{A_2}, L_1, L_2, L_3, A_1) \\
A_3 &= f_{A_3}(U_{A_3}, L_1, L_2, L_3, A_1, A_2) \\
Y_1 &= f_{Y_1}(U_{Y_1}, L_1, L_2, L_3, A_1, A_2, A_3) \\
Y_2 &= f_{Y_2}(U_{Y_2}, L_1, L_2, L_3, A_1, A_2, A_3, Y_1) \\
Y_3 &= f_{Y_3}(U_{Y_3}, L_1, L_2, L_3, A_1, A_2, A_3, Y_1, Y_2)
\end{aligned}
$$

The arguments $(U_*)$ represent error terms—random variables that induce the joint distribution of the variables in the model. In this example every variable depends on all the variables before it: nothing has yet been assumed away.
